content: The text provided is a detailed acknowledgment and description of contributors, funding sources, and processes involved in the development of WHO guidelines on tuberculosis diagnostics. The development of the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis diagnostics involved contributions from a wide range of experts, consultants, and organizations across the globe. These individuals and institutions provided technical expertise, systematic reviews, and external evaluations to ensure the guidelines were comprehensive and evidence-based. Contributors and Technical Experts Key contributors included professionals from institutions such as Stellenbosch University in South Africa, the Ifakara Health Institute in Tanzania, the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom, the University of Birmingham in the United Kingdom, Tulane University in the United States, and the University of Ottawa in Canada. Additional technical expertise was provided by Daniela Cirillo from San Raffaele SRL in Milan, Italy; Luis Cuevas from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine; Nora Engel from Maastricht University in the Netherlands; Anisa Hajizadeh from McMaster University in Canada; Nazir Ismail from the National Institute for Communicable Diseases in South Africa; Tamara Lotfi from the American University of Beirut in Lebanon; Adam Penn-Nicholson and Samuel Schumacher from FIND in Geneva, Switzerland; Rosa Stalteri from McMaster University; and Elisabetta Walters from Stellenbosch University. Observers Observers included Karen Heichman from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation in Seattle, USA; Tamara Kredo from the South African Medical Research Council; Amy Piatek from USAID in Washington, USA; Morten Ruhwald from FIND in Geneva, Switzerland; Raynal Squires from the WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean in Cairo, Egypt; Wayne van Gemert from the Stop TB Partnership in Geneva, Switzerland; and Mohammed Yassin from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria in Geneva, Switzerland. Funding The development of these guidelines was supported by funding from USAID through the USAID–WHO consolidated grant (grant number US-2016–0961). The funding agency's views did not influence the content or development of the guidelines. WHO Steering Group The WHO steering group overseeing the development of the guidelines included Christopher Gilpin, Alexei Korobitsyn, Fuad Mirzayev, Wayne van Gemert, and Karin Weyer, all from the WHO Global TB Programme. The guidelines were prepared based on consensus reached during a GDG (Guideline Development Group) meeting convened by WHO via an online webinar on January 16, 2016. Guideline Development Group The Guideline Development Group was chaired by Jan Brozek from McMaster University in Canada, with members including Jeremiah Chakaya Muhwa from the Kenya Medical Research Institute, Gavin Churchyard from the Aurum Institute in South Africa, Daniela Maria Cirillo from San Raffaele Hospital in Italy, Paul Klatser from the Royal Tropical Institute in the Netherlands, Arata Kochi (independent consultant, Switzerland), Satoshi Mitarai from the Japan Anti-Tuberculosis Association, Beatrice Mutayoba from the Ministry of Health in Tanzania, Ingrid Oxley Oxland from Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University in South Africa, Thomas M. Shinnick (independent consultant, USA), Karen Steingart from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, Wendy Stevens from the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa, Francis Varaine from Médecins Sans Frontières in France, Anna Vassall from LSHTM in the United Kingdom, and Yasuhiro Yasutomi from the National Institutes of Biomedical Innovation, Health, and Nutrition in Japan. External Review Group The external review group included Kathleen England from the KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation in the Netherlands, Levan Gagnidze from the International Organization for Migration in Thailand, Rumina Hassan from Aga Khan University in Pakistan, Nazir Ismail from the National Institute for Communicable Diseases in South Africa, Richard Lumb from Adelaide TB SRL in Australia, Enos Masini from the National TB Programme in Kenya, Alaine Nyaruhirira from Management Sciences for Health in South Africa, Somsak Rienthong from Bangkok TB SRL in Thailand, Leen Rigouts from the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Belgium, and Maria Alice Telles from Management Sciences for Health in Brazil. Systematic Review Team The systematic review team was led by Adithya Cattamanchi from UCSF in the United States, with contributions from Katherine Farr, Priya B. Shete, Hojoon Sohn, and Luke Strnad, all from UCSF. The economic evaluation was led by Hojoon Sohn from McGill University in Canada. Additional Funding Additional funding was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and USAID through the USAID–WHO consolidated grant (grant number GHA-G-00-09-00003/US-2014-741). Development of Specific Diagnostic Sections The sections on loop-mediated isothermal amplification, first-line line probe assays, second-line line probe assays, and lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan assays were developed under the guidance of the WHO steering group. These sections were prepared by Christopher Gilpin, Alexei Korobitsyn, and other members of the WHO Global TB Programme, based on consensus achieved during GDG meetings held in Montreux, Switzerland, and other locations. Acknowledgments The WHO acknowledges the contributions of all individuals and organizations involved in the development of these guidelines. Their expertise and dedication have been instrumental in advancing the global fight against tuberculosis.
